sql.title: Find active users
sql.prompt: Return `name` and `email` for users whose status is `active`. Sort alphabetically by name.
hints: Filter rows before ordering.
Return only the requested columns.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY name;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT, status TEXT);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE status = 'active' ORDER BY name;

sql.title: Top three salaries
sql.prompt: Return the three highest-paid employees with their name and salary. Sort from highest to lowest salary.
hints: Use ORDER BY with descending direction.
Limit the result after sorting.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

sql.title: Count employees by department
sql.prompt: Return each department and the number of employees in it. Sort by employee count descending, then department name.
hints: Group rows by department.
COUNT(*) counts rows in each group.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department;

sql.title: Customers without orders
sql.prompt: Find every customer who has never placed an order. Return customer names in alphabetical order.
hints: Start with customers so unmatched customers can survive.
Look for a NULL order identifier after the join.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL ORDER BY c.name;

sql.title: Departments above the average
sql.prompt: Return departments whose average salary is greater than 75000. Include the department and rounded average salary, ordered highest first.
hints: Group before filtering groups.
HAVING filters aggregate results.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT department, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS average_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING AVG(salary) > 75000 ORDER BY average_salary DESC;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT department, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS average_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING AVG(salary) > 75000 ORDER BY average_salary DESC;

sql.title: Second-highest distinct salary
sql.prompt: Return the second-highest distinct salary. Return one column named `second_highest_salary`, or NULL if it does not exist.
hints: Remove duplicate salary values before selecting.
OFFSET can skip the highest value.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT (SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS second_highest_salary;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, salary INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT (SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS second_highest_salary;

sql.title: Build a running revenue total
sql.prompt: Return each order date, its amount, and the cumulative revenue through that date. Preserve chronological order.
hints: Use SUM as a window function.
The window ORDER BY controls the running sequence.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT order_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS running_revenue FROM orders ORDER BY order_date, id;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_date TEXT, amount INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT order_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS running_revenue FROM orders ORDER BY order_date, id;

sql.title: Latest order per customer
sql.prompt: Return each customer and their latest order amount. Customers without orders should not appear.
hints: Rank orders inside each customer partition.
Filter the ranked relation after calculating the window value.

editor.defaultQuery: WITH ranked_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, id DESC) AS position FROM orders) SELECT c.name, r.amount AS latest_amount FROM customers c JOIN ranked_orders r ON r.customer_id = c.id WHERE r.position = 1 ORDER BY c.name;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, order_date TEXT, amount INTEGER);
editor.solutionQuery: WITH ranked_orders AS (SELECT customer_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, id DESC) AS position FROM orders) SELECT c.name, r.amount AS latest_amount FROM customers c JOIN ranked_orders r ON r.customer_id = c.id WHERE r.position = 1 ORDER BY c.name;

sql.title: Weekly active retention
sql.prompt: For each signup week, count how many users returned during the following week. Return signup week and retained user count.
hints: Join activity back to users using user_id.
Compare activity dates to the signup date using SQLite date functions.

editor.defaultQuery: SELECT u.signup_week, COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS retained_users FROM users u JOIN activity a ON a.user_id = u.id AND a.activity_date >= date(u.signup_week, '+7 day') AND a.activity_date < date(u.signup_week, '+14 day') GROUP BY u.signup_week ORDER BY u.signup_week;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signup_week TEXT); CREATE TABLE activity (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER, activity_date TEXT);
editor.solutionQuery: SELECT u.signup_week, COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS retained_users FROM users u JOIN activity a ON a.user_id = u.id AND a.activity_date >= date(u.signup_week, '+7 day') AND a.activity_date < date(u.signup_week, '+14 day') GROUP BY u.signup_week ORDER BY u.signup_week;

sql.title: Find missing invoice numbers
sql.prompt: Return invoice numbers that are missing between the smallest and largest invoice number. Sort ascending.
hints: Generate a sequence with a recursive CTE.
Compare generated values against invoices with NOT EXISTS.

editor.defaultQuery: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(value) AS (SELECT MIN(invoice_no) FROM invoices UNION ALL SELECT value + 1 FROM numbers WHERE value < (SELECT MAX(invoice_no) FROM invoices)) SELECT value AS missing_invoice_no FROM numbers WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.invoice_no = numbers.value) ORDER BY value;
editor.schema: CREATE TABLE invoices (invoice_no INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer TEXT);
editor.solutionQuery: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(value) AS (SELECT MIN(invoice_no) FROM invoices UNION ALL SELECT value + 1 FROM numbers WHERE value < (SELECT MAX(invoice_no) FROM invoices)) SELECT value AS missing_invoice_no FROM numbers WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.invoice_no = numbers.value) ORDER BY value;
